notes: Circuit: 40mV source (#4) in series with R 30ohm (#0), then L 4mH (#1), then R 50ohm (#2) in parallel with C 20uF (#3), returning along the bottom rail to the source. The ground reference is the node between R30 and L: a vertical wire drops from that top-rail node at x~400 all the way down past the bottom rail to the GND symbol (#5) at (402,609). NET MAP: n1 = top-left rail: V-DC(#4) + terminal (top) and the left lead of R 30ohm. 0 = ground: right lead of R 30ohm, the vertical wire at x~400, left lead of L 4mH (all joined on the top rail at site S0), and the GND symbol stub below the bottom rail. n2 = top rail right of the inductor: L right lead + top of R 50ohm (site S1) + top plate of C 20uF. n3 = bottom rail: V-DC bottom (- terminal), bottom of R 50ohm (site S17), bottom plate of C 20uF. JUDGEMENT CALLS: S16 (402,576) CRITICAL - OVERRIDDEN from the tracer default 'junction' to a CROSSING, expressed as explicit edge groups [[4,33],[30,32]] because the site has degree 5 (the GND stub e33 is counted twice). e4 is the vertical running up to the top rail, e33 is the 6px stub continuing down to the GND symbol, e30 is the bottom rail heading left to the V-DC bottom, e32 is the bottom rail heading right to R50/C. Evidence: (a) inkmap at (402,576) shows a plain X - the vertical is a uniform 2-3px stroke that passes straight through the 2px horizontal rail with no thickening, no solder blob (a dot would be ~3x stroke width in both axes) and no arc; (b) the drafter's habit on this sheet is decisive - every intended connection here is drawn as a T (S0 vertical ending on the top rail, S1 R50 top lead ending on the top rail, S17 R50 bottom lead ending on the bottom rail, and the V-DC leads), and S16 is the ONLY place on the sheet where one stroke runs continuously across another; (c) electrics: reading S16 as a junction merges the bottom rail into ground, which puts both ends of the source loop on {V-, R30-right} so the source drives only R30, and leaves L, R50 and C as a dead sub-network carrying exactly zero current in every branch - a degenerate circuit no drafter would set as a problem. The crossing reading yields the standard series-parallel AC network V-R30-L-(R50||C), every element energised, which is plainly what is drawn. S0 (395,371) CRITICAL -> junction: the x~400 vertical ends on the top rail from below (T, deg 3); reading it as a crossing would strand the ground wire and leave the circuit with no reference. S1 (594,374) CRITICAL -> junction: R 50ohm top lead ends on the top rail (T); a crossing would strand R50's top terminal. S17 (600,579) CRITICAL -> junction: R 50ohm bottom lead ends on the bottom rail (T); a crossing would strand R50's bottom terminal. Non-critical sites S2, S6, S8, S9, S11, S12 are all handwritten value text ('30 ohm', '4mH', '50 ohm', '20uF') brushing wire or component ink and are left at the tracer default; none of them changes the netlist. PORTS: no fixes needed - every terminal already sits on a real lead. Checked the flagged 'unused port candidates': (468,397) and (520/529,397) on the inductor are the '4mH' label strokes, (620,501) on R50 and (756,468) on the capacitor are the '50 ohm' and '20uF' label strokes, and (175,486) on the V-DC is the tail of the '40mV' label - none of them is a lead. CLASSES: all confirmed - #4 is a circle with + over - (V-DC), #3 is two parallel plates (Capacitor), #1 is a 4-loop coil (Inductor). No bridges dropped, no merges, no manual nets. Result: 6 components, 4 nets, ERC clean.
